雅思周末复习 · 第 6 周（11 月 28 日 周六）

这周五天（11 月 23 日到 27 日）的内容都在这一页里，大概 60 分钟。建议顺序：单词 15 分钟，听写 10 分钟，听力表达 5 分钟，阅读 15 分钟，写作口语 15 分钟。不用联网，手机上也能用。

3. 听力表达回顾（5 分钟）

这周五天都是 BBC 6 Minute English，表达都选自节目里主持人专门讲解的词，共 24 个。中文默认隐藏，先自己想意思再点开。斜体是录音里的原句，前面是说话人。

完整音频和原文都在每天的早间页面里（11-23 到 11-27 早间），这里为了文件小没有再放进来。哪天表达忘得多，就回那天页面再听一遍。

周一 11月23日：BBC 6 Minute English：Are microplastics harming us?（微塑料）

  • marine 海洋的点击显示
    Becca: Marine describes anything related to, found in or produced by the sea.
  • emerging (evidence) 新出现的（证据）点击显示
    Becca: The adjective emerging describes something coming into view after being hidden, allowing it to develop or be better understood.
  • correlation 相关性，关联点击显示
    Becca: A correlation is a link or connection between two or more things.
  • a spike (in something) （数量）猛增点击显示
    Becca: here it means a sudden, sharp increase in something.
  • exposure 接触，暴露点击显示
    Becca: And exposure means to come into contact with something that may have an impact on you.

周二 11月24日：BBC 6 Minute English：How reading shapes your brain（阅读和大脑）

  • dedicated 专门的，专用的点击显示
    Becca: Dedicated here means designed and used for one particular purpose.
  • co-opt （强行）拿来用，征用点击显示
    Georgie: Co-opt here means to include someone or something, often against their will.
  • inevitably 不可避免地点击显示
    Becca: Inevitably means in a way that cannot be stopped or avoided.
  • intricate 复杂精细的点击显示
    Georgie: If something is intricate, it has lots of detail.

周三 11月25日：BBC 6 Minute English：Why are we all so stressed?（压力）

  • chronic 长期的，慢性的点击显示
    Becca: beginning with the adjective chronic, which means continuing for a long time.
  • burnout （工作过度导致的）身心俱疲点击显示
    Neil: Burnout is a feeling of physical or mental exhaustion caused by working too hard.
  • concentrate / sharpen the mind 让人头脑更清醒点击显示
    Becca: If you say that a difficult situation sharpens or concentrates someone's mind, you mean that it makes them think clearly.
  • nerves 紧张，焦虑（口语）点击显示
    Neil: Nerves are an informal word for worry or anxiety.
  • one-size-fits-all 一刀切的点击显示
    Becca: A one-size-fits-all approach tries to apply the same solution to all problems, rather than solving them individually.

周四 11月26日：BBC 6 Minute English：Is social media dead?（社交媒体）

  • shatter the illusion 打破幻想点击显示
    Pippa: To shatter an illusion is to destroy someone's misconceptions, causing them to realise an unpleasant reality.
  • cultural happening （代表一个时代的）文化现象点击显示
    Neil: A cultural happening is an event that embodies the values and interests of a particular social group at a particular time.
  • behemoth 巨头，庞然大物点击显示
    Pippa: A behemoth is an extremely large and powerful company or organisation.
  • novelty 新鲜玩意儿，新奇感点击显示
    Neil: A novelty is something which is new and unusual and therefore exciting.
  • gravitate towards 自然而然地被……吸引点击显示
    Pippa: if you gravitate towards something, you are naturally attracted to it.

周五 11月27日：BBC 6 Minute English：Is Gen Z getting less intelligent?（PISA 成绩）

  • disruption 打乱，中断点击显示
    Georgie: starting with disruption, which means stopping people doing what they normally do.
  • the elephant in the room 明摆着却没人提的问题点击显示
    Phil: The expression the elephant in the room is used to refer to something that's obvious, but nobody is talking about.
  • deteriorate 变差，恶化点击显示
    Georgie: If something deteriorates, it gets worse.
  • a steep drop 大幅下降点击显示
    Phil: A steep drop is a big fall.
  • a blanket ban 全面禁止点击显示
    Georgie: A blanket ban means completely stopping someone from doing something.

4. 阅读易错题回顾（15 分钟）

从这周五篇 G 类阅读里挑出最容易错的题，每篇 5 道，共 25 道。主要是标题干扰项、同义替换、NOT GIVEN 和 NO 的区别，还有填空的单复数和数字张冠李戴。先自己判断，再点开答案，对照原文那一句。

判断题口诀：原文说反了是 FALSE（观点题是 NO），原文没说是 NOT GIVEN。填空题记得核对单复数和字数要求，匹配题字母可以重复用。这周的阅读是我自己编写的题，答案和解析也是自编。

周一 Section 3：Tiny Forests 城市迷你森林（标题匹配 + 句子结尾匹配 + 句子填空）

第 4 题　Paragraph E 选哪个标题？
i A method that depends on crowding　ii Why price may be the wrong comparison　iii Lessons from protected sacred places　iv Doubts about the evidence and long-term survival　v How cities plan to pay for new forests　vi Reported gains for wildlife, weather and learning　vii The decline of the commercial timber industry　viii Volunteers who give up too soon

点开看答案和解析

答案：iv　Doubts about the evidence and long-term survival

Critics point out that many of these figures come from the organisations that promote the method rather than from independent research. ... the real test is what happens after twenty or thirty years.

E 段两点：数据来源不独立（doubts about the evidence），以及长期存活存疑。viii 只覆盖了段里一个细节，不是全段主旨，标题题要选概括整段的。

原文出处：Paragraph E

第 5 题　Paragraph F 选哪个标题？
i A method that depends on crowding　ii Why price may be the wrong comparison　iii Lessons from protected sacred places　iv Doubts about the evidence and long-term survival　v How cities plan to pay for new forests　vi Reported gains for wildlife, weather and learning　vii The decline of the commercial timber industry　viii Volunteers who give up too soon

点开看答案和解析

答案：ii　Why price may be the wrong comparison

Defenders reply that comparing the two is misleading. ... should not be judged by the same measure.

F 段先说成本高，再说这样比较有误导性，主旨是价格不一定是合适的比较标准。v 是陷阱：段里没讲城市怎么筹钱。

原文出处：Paragraph F

第 8 题　句子结尾匹配（A到F）：Some foresters believe the fast early growth of tiny forests ______
A. competition between them makes them grow quickly upwards.　B. will not provide results for some time.　C. store more carbon than any other type of forest.　D. are less able to survive storms, fire and disease than native woodland.　E. are usually paid for by local schools.　F. is mainly due to good soil and regular care.

点开看答案和解析

答案：F　is mainly due to good soil and regular care.

Some foresters argue that rapid early growth is hardly surprising, since any young tree grows quickly when it is given rich soil and regular watering

rich soil and regular watering = good soil and regular care。注意 hardly surprising 是“不奇怪”的意思。

原文出处：Paragraph E

第 12 题　句子填空（NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS）：During the first few years, volunteers water and ______ the site.

点开看答案和解析

答案：weed

Volunteers water and weed the site for the first two or three years

the first few years = the first two or three years。weed 这里是动词“除草”，不要写成 weeds。

原文出处：Paragraph C

第 14 题　句子填空（NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS）：Most observers agree that tiny forests cannot replace the protection of ______.

点开看答案和解析

答案：existing woodland / woodland

...tiny forests are no substitute for protecting existing woodland

no substitute for = cannot replace。existing woodland 两个词，只写 woodland 也算对。

原文出处：Paragraph G

周二 Section 1：Hillcrest 周末市集广告（信息匹配）+ 租房押金和房屋状况报告（句子填空）

第 3 题　哪个市集（A到E）：lets members of the public sell things without reserving a place in advance（字母可重复用）

点开看答案和解析

答案：E

…sell straight from your boot… with no booking needed: just pay at the gate.

without reserving a place in advance = no booking needed，选 E。D 也能摆摊，但必须提前两周订，正好是干扰项。

原文出处：Paragraph E

第 5 题　哪个市集（A到E）：offers a service that tells you how much your belongings are worth（字母可重复用）

点开看答案和解析

答案：B

Experienced dealers will value your old items for a small fee.

tells you how much your belongings are worth = value your old items，选 B。这题和第 1 题都是 B，字母可以重复用。

原文出处：Paragraph B

第 10 题　句子填空（NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER）：Tenants are sent a ______ which shows their bond number.

点开看答案和解析

答案：receipt

You will then be sent a receipt showing your bond number…

shows = showing，填 receipt。注意别填 bond number，空格后面已经有了。

原文出处：Paragraph F

5. 写作和口语回顾（15 分钟）

下面的范文和口语回答都是我自己写的参考答案，不是官方答案，目标 7 分左右。先别看，花 3 分钟口头说一下你会怎么写或者怎么讲，再点开对照。题目原话以你当天的任务为准。

周二大作文：房租暴涨带来的问题和解决办法（Task 2 问题解决类）

In many cities, the cost of renting a home has risen sharply in recent years. What problems does this cause? What measures could be taken to solve these problems?

点开看参考范文（约 264 词，目标 7 分左右）

In many cities, rents have climbed much faster than wages over the past decade. This essay will look at two main problems caused by this trend and suggest some practical measures that governments and employers could take.

The first problem is that young people find it almost impossible to save. When half of a monthly salary goes on rent, there is little left for a deposit on a home, so many people in their thirties still cannot afford to buy a flat. A second problem is that lower-income workers are pushed out to the suburbs. Nurses, cleaners and shop assistants often have to commute for over an hour each way, which leaves them exhausted and reduces their quality of life. In the long run, this also makes it harder for city hospitals and shops to find staff.

Several measures could ease these problems. To begin with, governments should build more affordable housing and offer it to key workers at below-market rents. They could also limit how much a landlord can raise the rent each year, so that tenants are able to plan their budgets. Another solution is for employers to play a part. Companies could provide housing allowances, or allow staff to work from home several days a week, which would let them live further away without a long daily commute.

In conclusion, rising rents make it hard for young people to save and force many workers to live far from their jobs. A combination of public housing, sensible rent controls and support from employers would go a long way towards solving these problems.

结构：开头改写题目，说明会讲两个问题和对应办法；第二段写两个问题，每个都说清后果；第三段给办法，写清楚谁来做、怎么做，并且和问题一一对上；结尾总结，不加新观点。问题解决类最常丢分的地方是只写问题或只写办法，两边都要写到。

可以背的句子：rents have climbed much faster than wages（房租涨得比工资快多了）；there is little left for a deposit（剩不下多少钱付首付）；are pushed out to the suburbs（被挤到郊区）；ease these problems（缓解这些问题）；go a long way towards solving（对解决问题大有帮助）。

周四书信：写给铁路公司失物招领处（正式书信）

You recently travelled on an overnight train and left a bag in your sleeping compartment. Write a letter to the railway company's lost property office. In your letter: give details of your journey; describe the bag and what was in it; explain how you would like the bag to be returned to you.

点开看参考范文（约 186 词，正式语气，不用缩写）

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to enquire about a bag that I left on one of your overnight trains last week.

I travelled on the 21:40 sleeper service from Sydney to Melbourne on Friday 20 November and arrived at Southern Cross Station at 7:15 the following morning. I was in sleeping compartment 14 in carriage C. Unfortunately, I was in a hurry to leave the train and only realised that my bag was missing when I reached my hotel.

The bag is a small dark blue backpack with a red luggage tag on one of the straps. Inside there are some clothes, a black laptop charger and a brown leather wallet. The wallet is particularly important, as it contains my driving licence and several bank cards.

If the bag has been found, I would be grateful if you could send it by courier to my home address, 12 Park Road, Ashfield, NSW 2131. I am happy to pay any delivery costs. Alternatively, I could collect it from Central Station in Sydney.

I would appreciate it if you could contact me on 0412 345 678 as soon as possible.

Yours faithfully,

Alex Lee

三个要点都覆盖了：第二段写行程（日期、车次、车站、车厢和包厢号），第三段写包的样子和里面的东西，并说明为什么急需，第四段写希望怎么寄回，愿意付运费，还给了另一个选择。正式信用 Dear Sir or Madam 开头，就要用 Yours faithfully 结尾。好用的句型：I am writing to enquire about…；I would be grateful if you could…；I would appreciate it if you could…

口语 Part 2 和 Part 3：本周三个话题

每个话题先自己连续说 1 到 2 分钟，再看示范，挑一两个表达用到你自己的答案里。示范里的经历是编的，换成你自己的真实经历，更容易说得自然。

11/23 口语 Part 2：Describe a place in nature that you enjoy visiting（点开看参考回答）

You should say: where it is, how often you go there, what you do there, and explain why you enjoy visiting this place.

Part 2 参考回答（约 195 词，大概说 2 分钟）：

I'd like to talk about a small lake in the hills, about an hour's drive from where I live. It isn't a famous tourist spot, so it's a bit off the beaten track, and that's exactly why I like it.

I usually go there about once a month, normally on a Sunday morning when the roads are quiet. I often go with a couple of friends, but sometimes I go on my own when I need some peace and quiet.

There's a path that goes all the way around the lake, so we walk for about two hours and then have a simple picnic on the grass. In autumn the trees turn red and yellow, and the only sounds you can hear are birds and the wind. Once we even saw a family of deer drinking at the edge of the water, which was unforgettable.

The main reason I enjoy it is that it helps me get away from it all. I spend most of my working day looking at a screen, so being surrounded by nature really recharges my batteries. When I drive home, I always feel calmer and ready for the week ahead.

Part 3 参考回答（当天的 4 道题）：

Why do people in cities like to spend time in nature?
I think it's mainly because city life is so busy and noisy. Being in nature gives people a break from traffic, crowds and work messages. Even a short walk in a park can make people feel less stressed, which is why so many city people go hiking at weekends just to clear their heads.

Should governments create more parks and green spaces in cities?
Yes, definitely. Parks are free, so everyone can use them, whatever their income. They also make the air cleaner and give children somewhere safe to play. In my city, an old car park near the station was turned into a small park, and now it's always full of families.

Do you think children today spend less time outdoors than in the past? Why?
Yes, I'm afraid so. When I was a kid, we played outside after school until it got dark, but nowadays many children spend their free time on tablets and games. Parents are also more worried about safety, so they prefer to keep their kids at home.

How can tourism damage natural places, and what can be done about it?
Too many visitors can leave rubbish, damage plants and frighten wild animals. On some popular mountains, the paths are badly worn away. One solution is to limit the number of visitors each day and charge a small entry fee, and then use that money to protect the area.

11/25 口语 Part 2：Describe a piece of useful advice someone gave you（点开看参考回答）

You should say: who gave you the advice, what the advice was, why they gave it to you, and explain why it was useful to you.

Part 2 参考回答（约 182 词，大概说 2 分钟）：

I'd like to talk about some advice my first manager gave me when I had just started working, about five years ago. She was very experienced and quite strict, but always fair.

In my first few months, I tried to make everything perfect, so I often stayed late and still missed deadlines. One evening she noticed I was stressed and told me, 'Finish first, then make it perfect.' She suggested that I send her a rough version early and improve it later.

She gave me that advice because she could see I was wasting a lot of time on small details that nobody really cared about. At first I was a bit embarrassed, but I decided to give it a try.

It turned out to be incredibly useful. I started finishing tasks on time, and her early feedback meant I didn't go off in the wrong direction. Looking back, I realise it made a real difference not only to my work but also to how I study now. Even for IELTS writing, I do a quick first draft and then improve it.

Part 3 参考回答（当天的 4 道题）：

Who do young people usually go to for advice, family or friends? Why?
I'd say friends, especially for everyday things like relationships or what to wear. Friends are the same age, so young people feel they understand them better. But for big decisions, such as choosing a university or a job, most still ask their parents, because parents have more life experience.

Is it a good idea to get advice from the internet?
It can be, but you have to be careful. The internet is great for practical questions, like how to fix a leaking tap. However, for health or money problems, a lot of the information online is unreliable, so it's better to check it with a professional.

Why do some people find it hard to accept advice?
Some people feel that advice is a kind of criticism, so they get defensive. Others are simply proud and want to solve problems by themselves. Also, if the advice is given in a rude way, people are less likely to listen, even when it's good advice.

Do you think older people always give better advice than younger people?
Not always. Older people have more experience with things like work and family, so their advice is often wiser. But on topics like technology or social media, younger people usually know much more. For example, my niece taught me how to protect my privacy online.

11/27 口语 Part 2：Describe a time when you helped someone（点开看参考回答）

You should say: who you helped, what the situation was, how you helped them, and explain how you felt after helping this person.

Part 2 参考回答（约 194 词，大概说 2 分钟）：

I'd like to talk about a time I helped an elderly neighbour of mine. It happened about two years ago, when a new management system was introduced in our apartment building.

Suddenly everything had to be done through an app: booking the laundry room, paying the building fee and even opening the parcel lockers. My neighbour is in his late seventies, and I could tell that he was really struggling with it. One day I saw him standing at the lockers for ages, looking confused.

So I offered to help. That weekend I went to his flat, set up the app on his phone and wrote down each step on a piece of paper in large letters. Then we practised together a few times until he got the hang of it. After that, I checked on him every couple of weeks.

Looking back, I felt really good about it, because it only took me a few hours, but it made his life much easier. He still thanks me every time we meet, and sometimes he brings me fruit from his hometown. It taught me that small actions can mean a lot to other people.

Part 3 参考回答（当天的 4 道题）：

Do people help each other less now than in the past? Why?
In some ways, yes. In big cities, many people don't even know their neighbours, so they're less likely to help them. On the other hand, the internet makes it easier to help strangers, for example through online donations, so I think the way people help has changed rather than disappeared.

Why do some people do volunteer work?
Most people volunteer because it makes them feel useful and happy. Some also want to meet new people or gain experience for their CV. For instance, a friend of mine volunteered at a food bank after she moved abroad, and it helped her make friends and improve her English.

Should schools teach children to help others? How?
Yes, I think they should, because kindness is a habit that's easier to build when you're young. Schools could organise simple projects, like visiting a care home or cleaning up a local park. Older students could also help younger ones with their reading.

Is it the government's job or individuals' job to help people in need?
I believe it's both. The government should provide a basic safety net, such as healthcare and unemployment benefits, because individuals can't do that alone. But individuals can offer things the government can't, like time, friendship and local knowledge, so the two should work together.

6. 自查清单

  • 主词表遮住中文，至少能说出 104 个意思（大约 85%）。
  • 15 个听写词至少对 12 个，错的抄三遍。
  • 24 个听力表达能说出中文意思，并且至少能用 5 个各造一句。
  • 阅读易错题每道都能指出原文对应句，说清楚错在哪：同义替换没认出来、标题选成细节、NOT GIVEN 当成 FALSE，还是填空拼写和字数。
  • 问题解决类大作文能说出四段式结构，每个问题都能对上一个办法，范文里“可以背的句子”能默写一半。
  • 能说清楚正式书信的开头结尾怎么配（Dear Sir or Madam 配 Yours faithfully），三个要点各写什么。
  • 三个口语 Part 2 话题各能连续说 1 分半钟以上，Part 3 每题能说 3 到 4 句。

写好的大作文、书信，或者口语录音转成的文字，直接发到聊天里，我帮你批改，告诉你大概几分、哪里可以改。
